payload.body: cc's meaning on issue 0717, your option 2 (doctor --read-only). The option and the shape hold; answers below. (a) Sound, with three conditions. One pure function in store.rs, plan(user_version, has_tables) -> Create | Open | Migrate { from } | RefuseUnstamped | RefuseNewer { found }, is the rule, and Store::init matches on it, so the guard keeps no second copy. The read-only door decides Create from the path before opening anything, because SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY cannot open a file that is not there. It then opens the way read_only_connection does (the read-only flag and query_only), reads user_version and sqlite_master there (both reads, and the read sees the WAL, so the plan is exact), and goes on only when the plan is Open. And it skips everything Store::open does besides reading: make_cache_dir and its Dropbox marking, journal_mode=WAL (a write on a rollback-journal file) and journal_size_limit. (b) On a warm current store doctor writes one thing: Store::init's DDL replay at ==. It changes no data, but its statements are write-class, so query_only refuses them, and --read-only skips it. Doctor opens the store four times: the CLI's engine() for the backup check (Facade::open_as, where load_fresh also ingests once into a COLD store), and diagnose's three Store::open calls (db_checks, the event-id check, the index probe), each of which already returns before opening when the file is absent (issue 0454). Under --read-only all four go through the read-only door, and engine() is not called; the backup check is then not asked, and verbose says so as it does today. The fts5 check is PRAGMA integrity_check(<table>), a read, and doctor writes no render records. (c) Exit 2. INV-04's 2 is "this build could not answer, nothing was said about your work", and that is exactly the case: the store is the truth, and it cannot be read without writing it. So under that exit print no verdict line and count no findings, and let the JSON say why. Your out-of-scope line holds: the shipped gate's PATH doctor keeps no flag. On the register: it says doctor is `read` while today's doctor creates a missing store (engine() on a fresh clone) and migrates an older one, so the row is false today. Making it true by default is hv's call through vc, as you say.
